title: The bus network decision
scenario: The transport department has produced a long options report. The mayor and cabinet decide on Friday and have only minutes to read. Write a precise briefing note with the essential points.

text: Three options for the regional bus network were assessed.

Option A, patching the existing network, would cost about 4 million a year and leave ridership flat. Roughly a third of the vehicles reach the end of their working life in 2029, and the replacement cost is not included in the figure.

Option B, a core-frequency network, concentrates service on the twelve busiest routes, running buses every ten minutes. It requires 11 million of capital spending over three years. Modelling suggests an increase of 18% in passengers on core routes. To pay for it, six low-use rural routes would be replaced by an on-demand minibus service, which has been well received in the one town where it was tested but remains unproven at scale.

Option C, a full redesign including new depots and traffic-priority lanes, would cost 24 million over five years and is projected to raise ridership by 30%. It would cause disruption on main roads for about three years. It depends on a state grant covering half of the cost; applications close on 30 September, and approval is not guaranteed.

The consultation received 3,200 responses, with a majority favouring more frequent services. Officers' view is that Option B delivers most of the benefit at the lowest risk, and that it can be designed so that a move to Option C remains possible if the grant is awarded.
The decision needed on Friday is whether to proceed with Option B and, separately, whether to submit the grant application for Option C before the deadline.

task.audience: the mayor and cabinet, who have a few minutes
task.prompt: Write a briefing note (90–140 words). Recommend an option, give the main benefit, the main cost or risk, and the deadline.

points.idea: Officers recommend Option B (11 million over three years).
B is expected to raise passengers on core routes by 18%.
The cost: six rural routes become an on-demand service, which is unproven at scale.
The grant application for Option C closes on 30 September and is uncertain.

model: Recommendation: proceed with Option B, the core-frequency network, at a capital cost of 11 million over three years. It keeps frequent service on the twelve busiest routes and is expected to raise core-route ridership by 18%, with the least risk of the three options. The main trade-off is that six low-use rural routes would be swapped for a minibus service on demand, which worked in one town but is unproven at scale. Option C offers more, 30% growth, but depends on a state grant that is not guaranteed. The grant application closes on 30 September, so a separate decision is needed on Friday. Option B can be designed to keep Option C possible.
useful: a separate decision is needed on …
can be designed to keep … possible
tips: For top decision makers, lead with the recommendation and keep to a handful of precise points: benefit, trade-off, deadline. Everything else is on request.
Make the decision in front of them explicit, including any decision that is separate (the grant) and its date.
explain: The note needs the recommended option and its cost, the headline benefit, the rural-route trade-off and uncertainty, and the grant deadline. The number of consultation responses is supporting evidence that does not change the decision.
